title: Integrating machine learning and spatiotemporal transcriptomics to build a diagnostic model for osteosarcoma metastasis and to decipher the role of necroptosis genes.
summary: A glmBoost+Ridge model selected seven genes from public osteosarcoma transcriptomic data to classify metastatic status; the paper reports AUC 0.861 in training and 0.873 in validation, plus RT-qPCR comparison across four cell lines. This is a retrospective computational diagnostic result with preliminary cell-line support, not a clinically validated diagnostic or causal mechanism.
ai_technology: The authors compare 113 algorithm/regularization combinations and select glmBoost+Ridge to classify metastatic versus nonmetastatic samples from transcriptomic features
organization: Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Jinan, China; Affiliated Hospital of Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Jinan, China

evidence.tested: A glmBoost+Ridge model selected seven genes from public osteosarcoma transcriptomic data to classify metastatic status; the paper reports AUC 0.861 in training and 0.873 in validation, plus RT-qPCR comparison across four cell lines. This is a retrospective computational diagnostic result with preliminary cell-line support, not a clinically validated diagnostic or causal mechanism. Evaluation: Retrospective public GEO/TCGA cohorts use a held-out validation set and consistent preprocessing; RT-qPCR across four established cell lines is limited in-vitro support. Authors state larger prospective multicenter validation and in-vivo causal testing are still needed.
evidence.unknown: The classification used retrospective public cohorts and four cell lines; prospective validation and in-vivo causal effects remain untested.
evidence.ai_role: The authors compare 113 algorithm/regularization combinations and select glmBoost+Ridge to classify metastatic versus nonmetastatic samples from transcriptomic features.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
